The structure is in place.
The visual refinement needs work.

The available development screenshots broadly follow the reference layout. They still differ substantially in typography, surface depth, selection emphasis, composer spacing and control hierarchy. The current direction adds a contextual action shelf in place of the single Send slot, alongside stronger accents and selective rounding. One open-toolbar capture also shows a concrete overlap defect.

Owner clarification · 22 October 2026. The interface should have more depth, stronger accents and more selective rounding. A selected tab defaults to a light grey or white fill with black text, unless the user explicitly overrides its accent colour. A generic blue theme fallback does not constitute that explicit override. This supersedes the earlier report's broad acceptance of blue selection styling for tabs.

The change concerns selected tabs specifically. Keyboard focus, selected conversation rows and other control states retain their own roles; the clarification does not automatically give all of them the same white treatment. Strong surface separation and appropriately rounded containers should make the interface feel more dimensional while keeping secondary content calm.

What this review establishes. Direct observations of the pictured builds, supported by the accompanying development emails. The pack contains nine image files and eight distinct images; reference 06 is a byte-identical copy of reference 04.

What “latest” means here. E053 is the latest available focused Spaces capture, attached to the 21 October 13:51 email. E073 is the latest attached image overall, captured at 00:18 on 22 October, but it shows Home and Account settings. The 01:34 update reports a newer ARM preview and further changes without a fresh screenshot. This report therefore does not certify the newest source or live application.

Confidence: high for the visible comparisons; limited for unpictured states and later fixes. A numerical fidelity percentage would imply a precision these different viewports, themes and states cannot support.

1. Current direction: a contextual composer action shelf

Owner direction · 22 October 2026. Replace the single Send slot with horizontally overlapping icon buttons: the primary stays fully visible on the left; the next is tucked almost completely behind it, leaving only a narrow sliver of its right edge and a tiny glimpse of its icon visible. The accepted final preview is more tightly tucked than the earlier versions. Horizontal or vertical scrolling still swaps the front action; scroll direction does not change the horizontal layout. Position dots show the current place while scrolling.

The shelf contains a maximum of five eligible items. Five is a ceiling, not a target: actions appear only when the current context requires them. Do not add placeholders, repeat actions or invent an extra action to fill the shelf. Where there is no next eligible item, do not fabricate a right-hand preview.

This is a new design direction for a future implementation. None of the historical screenshots below demonstrates this shelf. The report records the direction; it does not change the application or living specification.

Approved design preview · simulated interactions

The accepted, tightly tucked horizontal shelf

The preview uses a 56 × 56 px primary button, with the next button extending only 14 px beyond its right edge: a 70 px total footprint. This is an overlap, not a gap between buttons. The secondary icon remains mostly concealed. These measurements record the approved preview; preserve its visual proportions when adapting it to production sizes and input methods.

Use the conversation-state selector to inspect the three defined scenarios. Scrolling either axis or pressing the rear peek brings another action forward; pressing the front button activates it. Dots appear during navigation. The preview simulates Stop / Resume timing, Voice and queuing locally. It does not demonstrate application integration, actual runtime acknowledgement, microphone access or durable persistence.

Owner-defined scenarios and exact order

Current contextEligible actions, in orderPrimary left / tightly tucked next action rightMeaning
Idle chat with a draftSend → VoiceSend / VoiceSend is the first action. Stop is absent because no agent pass is running. Only these two items appear for this scenario.
Running agent with a draftSteer → Stop → Queue → VoiceSteer / StopThe draft can steer the running pass or be queued. Stop remains a distinct runtime action. This scenario has four items, not five.
User stopped mid-responseResume → End PassResume / End PassAfter the runtime acknowledges the stop, the preserved pass is resumably paused. Resume continues it; End Pass ends that pass terminally.

Action semantics and runtime truth

ActionSemantic roleBoundary to preserve
SendSubmit the draft from an idle chat.Its appearance in the first scenario does not justify showing it in every runtime state.
SteerUse the draft to redirect the currently running agent pass.Keep this distinct from queuing a later instruction.
StopRequest that the current response stop at a resumable paused state.Do not present a confirmed paused state, or the confirmed Resume / End Pass shelf, before runtime acknowledgement.
QueueQueue the draft for subsequent handling rather than immediately steering the active pass.Keep queued intent and current execution visibly distinct.
VoiceEnter the existing same-session Voice & Vision workflow.Retain genuine capture permissions and session ownership; shelf navigation alone must not start capture.
ResumeContinue the preserved, acknowledged paused pass.A pending or failed stop request is not an acknowledged paused pass.
End PassEnd the paused pass terminally.Keep it distinct from resumable Stop. Preserve existing draft and queued content; queue disposition is unspecified, so do not infer automatic execution or deletion.

Stopping is a runtime transition, not an instant visual claim. While acknowledgement is pending, show the real stopping state. If the request fails or is still pending, retain truthful status rather than announcing that the pass is paused. This direction does not claim that arbitrary external tool processes can pause: their supported cancellation, completion and other outcomes must be represented separately and accurately.

Proposed interaction rules · recommendations, not additional owner decisions

Make browsing safe and the active action predictable

  • Browsing never activates an action. Wheel/trackpad scrolling, touch swipes, keyboard browsing and pressing the rear peek only change the front item. The front button executes the selected action. Activation requires a deliberate press or the equivalent explicit keyboard command.
  • Preserve the draft. Browsing the shelf must not alter its text, attachments, selection or saved state. Stop, Resume, End Pass and Voice must not silently discard a draft; any intended submission transition follows the owning draft lifecycle.
  • Protect the action identity during a press. Bind activation to the action present when the press begins. If an external state update changes it or makes it ineligible, cancel the pending activation rather than dispatching a different action under the same release. Intentional scrolling or swiping can change the front item, but completing that browsing gesture must not execute it. Suppress accidental repeated activation across an action replacement, so a double-click on Send cannot also Stop the newly started pass, or End Pass also submit a preserved draft.
  • Choose wrap or no-wrap deliberately. This remains a proposed interaction choice. The illustrative preview uses wrap to keep a narrow sliver of the next action peeking out to the right; stopping at the list ends is an alternative. Acceptance of the tightly tucked appearance does not resolve this interaction choice. Neither choice adds items. Dots reflect the current position and actual eligible count during scrolling, never five fixed empty positions.
  • Provide keyboard and touch alternatives. Support deliberate browsing and activation without a mouse wheel, with visible focus, meaningful action names and an announced position/count. With a shelf button focused, arrow keys can browse. Enter/Space on the front button activates its action; on the rear peek, it brings the next action forward. With the text field focused, Enter follows the editor's own send/newline rules; do not silently redirect it to whichever shelf action was browsed. Avoid capturing unrelated page scrolling outside the shelf.
  • Keep Stop discoverable while an agent runs. It is the second item, with only a narrow sliver peeking to the right of Steer, in the defined running-with-draft order. Preserve a clear, quickly reachable route to Stop after browsing; gesture-only discovery is insufficient. Any accessible shortcut activates that same Stop action, not an extra shelf item. Keep usable touch targets and accessible names even though the visible rear button is tightly concealed.

Proposed eligibility for two other contexts: idle chat with an empty draft could show Voice only; a running agent without a draft could show Stop → Voice. These are suggestions for review, separate from the three owner-defined orders above. A single eligible action does not need an invented second item.

The tightly tucked visual arrangement is accepted, and the three owner-defined scenario orders are exact. Production rendering and runtime integration remain unverified. Wrap behaviour and the separately labelled interaction proposals still need review. There is no mandatory five-item inventory or invented extra action.

2. Main Spaces comparison

The strongest comparison is the expanded Professional reference against the focused Spaces draft. Both expose the composer, sidebar and shell. Conversation contents, model readiness, viewport size and host browser chrome differ.

Click an image to enlarge it. The full original images are embedded without retouching. The side-by-side cards scale each image to fit; measurements below refer to the original pixels.

What already aligns

  • The rail is approximately 70 pixels wide and the contextual sidebar approximately 280 pixels wide in both source images. Their different share of the window mainly follows the different overall widths.
  • The expanded composer is a continuous rounded surface with draft text above the lower controls. The circular upward Send matches the historical reference; the new action shelf supersedes that single-action slot for future design.
  • The actual app has a clear selected chat row and a separate main working surface. Its wider toolbar capture also shows substantially more balanced composer margins.
  • Browser tabs, the address bar, emoji and additional app entries can coexist with this layout. Their presence does not prevent a faithful visual system.

3. Detailed findings and corrections

Priority 1 · observed defect

The formatting toolbar overlaps model recovery

In E038 the Aa popup covers part of Manage local models. A hard-edged dark backing extends around the rounded formatting buttons. The email explicitly confirms the remaining status-row overlap and dark corners. Source: E038

Correction: lay out the toolbar against the actual composer and status-row bounds, with enough separation to keep every action usable. Give the outer popup its intended rounded surface. Recheck with recovery present, a multiline draft, narrow width and increased text scale.

Evidence limit: E053 shows the toolbar closed. It cannot prove this was fixed later. The toolbar itself is an intended newer feature and should be retained.

Priority 2 · spacing

The composer loses its margins in the narrower capture

Reference 02 has roughly 84 pixels on the left and 83 on the right between the composer and the main work-area edges. E053 has approximately 12 and 18 pixels. The input and recovery text consequently feel pressed against the sidebar and window edge. Reference 02 · E053

Correction: set an intentional responsive minimum gutter together with a maximum composer width; align the recovery row to the same content bounds. Test the behaviour with the sidebar open at both narrower and wider widths.

These are bitmap measurements from 1530- and 1280-pixel-wide images, not a specification to impose fixed 84-pixel margins everywhere. The wider E038 composition is already closer. Two stills alone do not prove the exact breakpoint or source of the narrower behaviour.

Priority 2 · typography

Navigation and controls lack the reference's hierarchy

The reference gives Chat, its filled bubble, primary navigation and section labels substantial size and weight. E053 uses a small plain Chat heading and smaller, lighter navigation, status text and shell controls. The large empty-state greeting dominates while the repeated working controls feel comparatively weak. Image comparison

Correction: reconcile the shared text roles for Space title, primary action, section label, conversation title and secondary metadata. Make chat titles more distinct from timestamps, and give the Space identity appropriate prominence. Inspect the actual font loaded before diagnosing a font-family problem; pixels alone cannot establish that.

The empty-state greeting and synthetic chat titles are legitimate state differences. Improving hierarchy does not require copying the reference's restaurant conversation or making every label bold.

Priority 2 · current design requirement

Selected tabs need a decisive default treatment

The owner's clarification requires a light grey or white selected tab with black text by default. It should remain immediately recognisable against the dark tab strip after the pointer moves away. A muted blue selected fill is not the required fallback. Current owner direction

Correction: use the neutral selected-tab treatment when there is no explicit user accent override. When an override exists, honour it and retain a clearly legible foreground. Keep unselected, hovered, selected and keyboard-focused states distinguishable. A blue focus ring can remain a separate focus cue; it does not replace the selected fill.

Acceptance: show the default selected tab, an unselected tab, hover, keyboard focus and a user-overridden accent on the same build. Remove the override and confirm the neutral default returns. Do not infer that a single historic still demonstrates all of these states.

Priority 2 · surfaces

The captured palette changes the visual balance

The reference uses a lifted charcoal composer against a dark workspace. E053 has an almost-black workspace, a much darker composer and a comparatively brighter sidebar. Its blue focus outline defines the input more strongly than its fill. Image comparison

Priority 2 · shared controls

The top-bar controls need stronger visual treatment

The reference uses substantial rounded model/status, search, notification and profile controls. The actual shared cluster is a row of small bare symbols. That lowers immediate legibility and makes the model control less informative. The newer E073 capture does place Profile at the far right, so the older E053 order should not be described as the final order. E053 · E073

Correction: preserve the later Haven address-bar location and give the controls a coherent apparent size, spacing, shape and hierarchy. Display genuine model/system state according to the current design. The later CPU/percentage direction takes precedence over copying the illustrative Qwen pill. Host placement: E026 · Profile work: E056 · Shared styling: E064

A small glyph does not establish a small click target. The no-model test state also does not justify inventing a utilisation percentage or account picture.

Priority 3 · consistency and clarity

Composer icons and policy state need a coherent hierarchy

E053 mixes a heavy exposed plus, thin Aa, outlined emoji, a small sliders symbol and circular Send. The reference's visible Ask for Approval label communicates more immediate policy information than the actual unlabeled sliders icon. Its semantics cannot be determined from a still. Image comparison

Correction: balance icon weight, size and alignment across the composer, and show the current permission policy in a clear, discoverable way appropriate to the latest design. Replace the pictured single Send slot with the new contextual action shelf; the screenshot remains evidence of the older control treatment. Verify the opened permission menu rather than assuming the sliders control implements a particular policy.

Known later change: E053 explicitly reports the plus reduced from 28 to 22 pixels in source, with the click target retained; this image still shows the old larger version. Recheck its rendered result before requesting the same change again. Source: E053

The historic handoff left the exact approval semantics unresolved. Model-choice approval tests in E041 do not establish the full composer permission UI. The extra emoji control and floating formatting bar are valid later additions.

Priority 3 · navigation and geometry

Restore clearer Space identity and verify the missing direct routes

The reference shows Chat Groups and Specialists as direct sidebar actions. They are not visible in E053, which shows New chat and recent conversations. Because the sidebar is customisable, this establishes a discoverability difference in the pictured configuration; it does not prove those features were deleted.

Correction: demonstrate those routes in the current sidebar/menu configuration and restore clear primary-action and section hierarchy. The broad workspace's upper-left join also appears much tighter than the reference. Give large containers, tabs, the composer and popup backing appropriate rounded geometry, scaled to their size and role.

Selective rounding: soften conspicuously square edges while preserving a hierarchy of shapes. Compact rows and dense toolbars can use smaller radii; large work surfaces and popovers can be more generous. Existing circular actions can remain circular. Avoid forcing every row, nested panel or toolbar into the same pill shape. Rounding must preserve alignment, usable width and the relationship between a container and its children. Current owner direction

Keep truthful model-recovery messaging. Its appearance should align with the composer and avoid collisions; different error states do not need the reference's exact Resolve Issues wording.

6. Additional refinement visible in later screenshots

These observations concern newer surfaces outside the supplied Chat mockups. They should be evaluated on their own terms.

  • Profile placement has progressed: E073 puts it at the far right. The shared controls still appear small and utilitarian relative to the reference.
  • Menu wording is repetitive: “Switch & Manage Users” appears in consecutive section/action lines. This is a visible clarity issue; it is not proof of duplicate backend handlers.
  • Identity naming needs confirmation: the Account title reads “CAKE ID account.” Confirm whether this is intended identity-service branding or legacy wording.
  • Some functions remain openly incomplete in that capture: the Account explanation says profile edits, plan, billing, username availability and icon upload are not connected.
  • Existing icon rendering needs refinement: the launcher has inconsistent weights and some fallback-looking box-X glyphs. These belong to the old pictured set and do not establish the quality of the incoming icon pack.

The email reports a successful first-close test; the still shows the windows before closing. It is evidence of the displayed state, with test outcome supplied separately by E073.

7. Recommended acceptance sequence

The next review should use one identified build, an explicit theme/variant and matched display scaling. This avoids reopening fixes already made after the last attached screenshot.

  1. Recheck the actual collision first. Open Aa with model recovery visible and verify the popup backing and all actions at ordinary and increased text scale.
  2. Stabilise responsive composer bounds. Compare wide and narrow windows with the sidebar open, preserving minimum margins and shared status alignment.
  3. Strengthen selection and surface depth. Verify the neutral selected-tab default and explicit accent override, distinguish hover from selection and focus, and give the composer and floating controls a clear place in the surface hierarchy.
  4. Reconcile typography and selective rounding. Align title/action/metadata roles, confirm the intended Professional variant, soften the appropriate large-container and popup edges and preserve compact geometry where it serves the content.
  5. Refine the global and composer controls. Keep Haven placement, verify the newer plus size, use consistent icon weight and show genuine model/permission state. Apply the new action shelf instead of reinstating the old single Send slot.
  6. Verify the shelf's exact scenarios and runtime transitions. Show Send → Voice for idle chat with a draft; Steer → Stop → Queue → Voice for a running agent with a draft; and Resume → End Pass after an acknowledged mid-response stop. Match the accepted tightly tucked appearance: the primary fully visible left, with only a narrow sliver and tiny icon glimpse of the next button visible right. Check either-axis scrolling, navigation dots and a maximum of five eligible items without filler. Demonstrate that a pending stop is not falsely presented as paused and that End Pass is distinct from resumable Stop, without inferring queue execution or deletion.
  7. Review the proposed interaction rules. Confirm that browsing does not activate, draft state survives, keyboard/touch alternatives work, Stop stays discoverable and changing runtime state cannot swap an action under a held pointer or active gesture. Review wrapping, proposed empty-draft eligibility and the distinction between text-field Enter and shelf-focused activation.
  8. Capture other missing states. Include empty compact input and Voice entry where eligible, focused expanded input, toolbar open, eligible action availability, a real populated conversation, the resource picker with a real attachment, the permission menu and a Summary with genuine activity.
  9. Review the remaining products and theme separately. Capture the running Present editor, accepted new app icons and identified Glow states. Use runtime/video evidence for hover and motion behaviour.

Acceptance position: retain the recognisable layout and legitimate newer features. Refine the shared visual system and demonstrated defects, then make surface-specific acceptance decisions from fresh comparable captures. The supplied evidence does not yet support calling the interface a complete visual match.

8. Evidence and method

This comparison uses the user-supplied 9to1_Spaces_UI_Reference_Pack_2026-10-12 (1).zip, including its manifest and historical handoff, and the previously consolidated 75-email development record through the 22 October 01:34 update. Eight distinct reference images and the relevant actual captures are embedded above.

The source-image comparison is independent of the emails' completion language. Email reports are identified as reports; visible states are identified as screenshots. The user's follow-ups on 22 October supply the current direction for stronger accents, neutral selected-tab defaults, selective rounding and the contextual composer action shelf, and supersede conflicting older guidance for those points. The shelf's three scenario orders and final tightly tucked visual arrangement are owner decisions; the separately labelled interaction recommendations are proposals. The embedded shelf is an approved design preview with simulated interactions, separate from the historical application screenshots. The linked living specification documents were not opened for this visual review. This report was revised; no application code, living specification, live service or worker instruction was changed.
